title: Defense Budget and Acquisition: Research & Analysis | CSIS
text:
Defense Budget and Acquisition

CSIS experts track the foremost budget issues in the defense policy sphere, exploring trends in the overall defense budget, military readiness, force structure, defense acquisition, and military compensation in a broader effort to assess the alignment of the country’s defense strategy and its resources.

How Quickly Can the DOD Rebuild and Recast the Munitions Industrial Base?

The U.S. munitions industrial base must be rebuilt and recast for modern wars of precision and attrition. By analyzing DOD budget documents and industry announcements, Dr. Jerry McGinn clarifies the planned future and remaining challenges to achieving this goal.

As the October 1 start of the fiscal year (FY) approaches, Congress has yet to enact defense funding for FY 2027. Seamus Daniels outlines the current status of legislation in response to the Trump administration’s $1.5 trillion defense budget request.

Are SBIR “Mills” Truly a Problem?

The Small Business Innovation Research Program has faced suggestions that a small number of “mills” receive a disproportionate share of awards while underperforming on innovation and commercialization metrics. An analysis of grant recipient data suggests this pattern reflects a division between specialized defense research contractors and dual-use venture-backed companies.

The Iran war has exacerbated the Pentagon’s shortage of key munitions, but it is not the only cause. There are also longstanding strategic, operational, and institutional reasons.

Reindustrialization and Great Power Competition: Deterrence by Capacity

The United States uses more munitions than are stockpiled, and its adversaries are noticing. In this piece, Dr. Benjamin Jensen argues that using capacity, a coefficient of deterrence, can alter the time horizon to solve the "empty bins" problem in Washington.
